St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firwsood, Trafford, will close down in August 2027. One mother told the BBC she feared she might not be able to get a place for her daughter at another local Catholic school. The council said falling pupil numbers had made the school's finances unsustainable. Council figures show more than 50 pupils secured places at other primary schools before the decision, leaving just 39 on its roll. Helen Fitzpatrick, 39, whose daughter Delilah attends St Teresa's, said families were "absolutely devastated" by the decision, announced on Monday. Fitzpatrick, who helped organise a campaign against the closure, said she had contacted nearby St Ann's RC Primary School but was told it could not guarantee Delilah a place for September 2027. Although a place was available when she enquired, she said she would have had to accept it immediately. "Delilah isn't ready to leave St Teresa's until it closes," she said. She said she feared Delilah could "get lost in the crowd" at a larger school. Delilah said she was "very sad" about the school closing. Image caption, Helen fears she may struggle to secure a place at another nearby Catholic school for her eight-year-old daughter Delilah Another parent, Sue Green, said she faced a similar dilemma over her five-year-old daughter Bethany. title: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected

input.lead: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.summary: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
input.evidence_text: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Plans for a 17-storey tower block next to a historic Manchester pub have been rejected by councillors. Developer The McGoff Group had applied to build 153 flats beside the Grade II-listed Marble Arch on Rochdale Road, which has been serving customers since 1888. The company said the scheme would deliver much-needed city centre housing and help regenerate the area. But the pub's owners argued the development threatened its future, and Manchester City Council's planning committee voted to refuse the application. In its objection, the pub said the 17-storey building would be "overbearing and oppressive" and would harm the setting of the pub. Councillors also raised concerns about the impact of the development on the Marble Arch and the lack of affordable housing in the scheme. Councillor Jon-Connor Lyons said he was "deeply concerned" about the effect on "one of Manchester's distinctive and much-loved historic pubs". A member of staff told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "We get tourists coming from all over the world who are sent here. "We have generations of families drinking here, dads and grandads and sons. You don't get places like this anymore and it's something we want to keep going." title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'

input.lead: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
input.summary: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
input.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

input.evidence_text: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss - BBC News Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October By Naj Modak , North West and Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 22 October 2026 Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said. Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport. He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk". As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning. The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs. In Salford, 41 properties were targeted with three in Tameside and two in Stockport over the period. Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Windows are seen boarded up on one property due to concerns of further attacks According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti. input.summary: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears

The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
